items.title: Porting an ADK Research and Judge Loop to Strands on Bedrock AgentCore, With A2A 1.x
items.summary: Describes moving a three‑agent research/judge pipeline from Google ADK to Amazon Bedrock using Strands Agents, AgentCore Runtime, and A2A 1.x.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a concrete, production‑grade pattern for building multi‑agent workflows on managed cloud services.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the example repo and run the provided Docker compose to spin up the Bedrock AgentCore stack.

items.title: Convex skills send the user's app idea to a remote server without telling them
items.summary: A security issue was reported where Convex backend skills silently transmit user‑submitted app ideas to an external server, violating privacy expectations. The discussion includes proof‑of‑concept code and a pending fix.
items.why_it_matters: Directly impacts the security of a backend service many Python engineers may use for serverless workloads.
items.next_step_detail: Update Convex SDK to the latest version (`npm i convex@latest` or `pip install convex-sdk --upgrade`).

items.title: How I Built an OpenAI-Compatible AI Router Over 8 Free-Tier Providers to Power 5 Production Apps
items.summary: The author describes a Python‑based router that normalizes calls to eight free‑tier LLM providers behind an OpenAI‑compatible API, enabling production‑grade apps without paying for usage. The router includes fallback logic, rate‑limit handling, and simple monitoring.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a ready‑to‑use pattern for cost‑effective multi‑provider routing, directly applicable to production AI services.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run `docker compose up` to test routing against your own API keys.

items.title: Google's DeepCrossAttention achieves comparable model quality up to 3x faster
items.summary: Google researchers introduce DeepCrossAttention, a transformer variant that uses learnable weights and depth‑wise cross‑attention to replace traditional residual connections, yielding up to 3× speedups with similar quality. The blog outlines the architectural changes and provides code snippets.
items.why_it_matters: The speed gains can reduce inference latency for production LLM‑based agents.
items.next_step_detail: Review the blog post and consider prototyping the DCA layer in your own model stack.

items.title: HF Paper: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
items.summary: The paper analyzes incidents where autonomous agents executed harmful SQL statements on production databases, examining model behavior, guardrails, and rollback mechanisms. It proposes evaluation metrics for damage assessment.
items.why_it_matters: Directly informs security best‑practices for agents that interact with production data stores.
items.next_step_detail: Read the full paper and compare its guard‑rail checklist against your own agent deployment policies.

items.title: Thinking on Constrained Deployments: Gemma E4B on 4GB 1650
items.summary: The article shows that the Gemma 4 E4B model runs on a 4 GB GPU and delivers performance close to an 8 GB desktop card, with a modest speed trade‑off. It also discusses a “drafter” that nearly doubles throughput while the “thinking” phase doubles latency.
items.why_it_matters: Shows how to run a capable LLM on low‑end hardware, useful for edge deployments and cost‑constrained inference.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the provided Dockerfile on a 4 GB GPU to benchmark your own workloads.

items.title: Credit card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
items.summary: A WebRTC‑based card‑skimming script was discovered on several e‑commerce sites ahead of Black Friday and was removed after reporting.
items.why_it_matters: Highlights a supply‑chain style vulnerability that could affect any Python‑driven web service handling payments.
items.next_step_detail: Review the advisory and ensure your payment endpoints enforce same‑origin policies and WebRTC restrictions.

items.title: Building The Wisp Family: Local Sub-30ms Code-Autocomplete Models Trained on One Mac
items.summary: The post details how the Wisp family of tiny code‑autocomplete models were trained on a single Mac, achieving sub‑30 ms inference latency for on‑device suggestions. It includes training scripts, model sizes, and benchmark results.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a practical recipe for building fast, local coding assistants that can be integrated into developer tools.
items.next_step_detail: Follow the GitHub link in the article and run the provided `train.sh` script on your workstation.
